title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 26 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: allies & theaters and capital: vc, m&a & ipos.

stories.h: DOW Commits $150M Conditional Loan to LeoLabs to Scale Space Radar Production
stories.what: Matched by private co-investment, the financing would fund two U.S. radar plants by 2028 and new sensors for LeoLabs' network by 2030.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Ukraine hits two Russian Iskander launchers in Bryansk region
stories.what: Ukraine’s armed forces have hit two Russian Iskander ballistic missile launchers and a Pantsir-S1 air defense system in Russia’s Bryansk region, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said on November 7.
stories.you: Allies' wars and budgets are the testing ground and a big second market for new defense tech.

stories.h: Japan to get new factory for US-2 flying boats by 2029
stories.what: Japanese aircraft maker ShinMaywa Industries will build a new factory on Kobe Airport Island to assemble the US-2 search-and-rescue flying boat it supplies to Japan’s Ministry of Defense, the company said at its latest earnings briefing.
stories.you: Being able to produce at scale has become a competitive edge in its own right; factories are now a venture category.

stories.h: Ukrainian Officials: F-16 ‘Super Effective’ at Downing Russia Drones But Challenges Remain
stories.what: Ukraine’s fleet of F-16 fighters has played a vital role in protecting the country against Russian aerial attacks, including the jet-powered drones the Russians have used to try to overpower Ukrainian air defenses, senior Ukrainian officials said.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: 'Permanent, serious' dialogue needed with China on AI: tech-focused lawmaker
stories.what: “The Chinese Communist Party doesn’t want rogue AI agents hacking their systems and their water authorities any more than we do,” Rep. James Walkinshaw, D-Va., said Thursday.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

watch.why: November 10. Could squeeze drone, motor and munitions supply weeks before the DoD ban.

idea.why: An autonomous interceptor under $5k for Shahed-class and FPV drones. Ukraine proved the concept, and Japan, the Gulf and US bases are buying. The cost-exchange crisis is acute.
